entries.english:
Co-plaintiff/applicant/intervenor: Johann Friedrich (Hund von Saulheim), master of the Order of St John in the German lands.

Co-defendants/intervenors: Konrad Freiherr von Boineburg, lord of Hohenburg, Bissingen, Bischhausen, and Erolzheim, imperial councillor, archducal Austrian privy councillor, president of the regimental government, and chamberlain of the Upper Austrian lands at Innsbruck; and Elias Pabst, Boineburg baronial chief bailiff, judge, and steward at Bissingen.

Plaintiff's attorneys: Dr. Johann Jakob Kölblin (1612); Lic. Guilielmus Fabricius (1622); Dr. Johann Konrad Albrecht (1623).
Defendant's attorneys: Lic. Wilhelm Fabricius (1618); Dr. Johann Georg Krapf (1622).

Subject of dispute (contemporary): mandate concerning distraint of 70 florins (withheld because of the appointment of the parish priest at Markt Bissingen); also concerning that appointment and the small tithe at Göllingen, Stillnau, Hohenstein, and Buggenhofen.

Subject of dispute (modern): dispute over appointment to the parish at Bissingen. In spring 1616 Hans Konrad von Rosenberg, Hospitaller commander at Kleinerdlingen, dismissed Christoph Laucher, the pastor nominated by the defendant baron, because he refused to issue the required written undertaking. With the baron's backing, however, Laucher remained in the parish for a further quarter-year. Since the commander withheld his stipend, the co-defendant steward distrained 70 florins from revenues belonging to the Order of St John from the small tithe at Göllingen, Stillnau, Hochstein, and Buggenhofen, and handed the money to the pastor.

The plaintiff master of the order viewed this as an attempt to dictate to the Order of St John concerning the appointment of the Bissingen pastor, and as interference with its possession of the tithe. The defendant baron argued that, despite the substantial tithe revenues attached to the parish, it carried only a small stipend; moreover, pastors were required to give an extremely unusual written undertaking, so resignations were frequent, as in Laucher's case. Because the plaintiff's party, which alternated with the opposing party in nominating a successor, had delayed, the defendant baron had asked Laucher to serve the parish through Easter. The tithe, which was subject to the baronial authority of Boineburg, was used to ensure that Laucher received his proper stipend.

Judgments in the proceedings were issued on 8 March 1619 and 8 March 1625.
Proceedings: Imperial Chamber Court, 1618–1625.

Also included: receipt by Christoph Laucher, pastor of Oberliezheim, for 75 florins, 1616 (item 10); schedule of the plaintiff's litigation costs (exhibit submitted 19 October 1625).

Contents and enclosures: process register, proceedings begun in 1618.
